verdict.rationale: Smithery runs a public registry of third-party MCP servers. Developers can search it and connect to its servers through the CLI (`smithery mcp search`, `tool find`), and connections go through a REST interface with OAuth apps Smithery maintains for popular integrations. Named catalog entries include Exa, Context7, Browserbase, Google Sheets and Brave Search, and an independent scan of the registry's 'top 100 servers' implies the catalog has more than 100 entries. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party count showing hundreds to thousands of integrations, and documentation of breadth across app categories beyond a handful of named examples.
